title: Zephyrine and the Confession
premise: When the coffin of town founder Aldous Zephyrine is exhumed for a memorial reinterment, it is found empty — and among his papers surfaces a will dated three days after his recorded death. Estate lawyer Emrys Winterbourne, who has privately solved three 'accidental' deaths no one else questioned, recognizes the handwriting of a dead clerk and realizes the confession hidden in the will implicates the town's founding families in a thirty-year-old murder. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Emrys traces swapped identities, forged alibis, and a living heir raised under another name, while someone begins silencing witnesses again. At the dinner she exposes the killer — the founder's own grandson, who emptied the coffin to destroy evidence of his grandfather's murder — and the true heir chooses justice over inheritance, ending with a quiet reburial and Emrys finally letting her own buried identity surface.
about_author: Odile Iversen is a former probate clerk from coastal Maine who spent a decade reading other people's last words before writing her own. She lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage with an untrustworthy cat named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Emrys Winterbourne's POV. Sorting the Zephyrine estate archives for the memorial reinterment, Emrys finds a will dated after Aldous Zephyrine's death, sealed in a clerk's hand she knows died decades ago. The legal impossibility thrills her old instinct for wrongness. Beat: curiosity sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The exhumation draws half the town to the churchyard; when the coffin lid lifts, it holds only river stones and a rotted glove. The mayor demands discretion; the gravedigger crosses himself. Emrys notices the stones came from the millrace, not the grave. Beat: public shock, private certainty that this was staged recently.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, flashback woven through present interviews. We learn how she quietly solved three deaths the police closed as accidents, and why she keeps her deductions off the record. A fourth name from those files now appears in the false will. Beat: establishing her method and her guilt about staying silent.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via invitation cards and gossip. In nine days the town celebrates the founding families' anniversary dinner, where the reinterment will be blessed. Emrys maps who benefits from the founder's myth: the Harrowgate brewery heirs, the Vane family, and Aldous's brittle grandson Caspian. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: A Clerk's Last Handwriting
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. She tracks the dead clerk Tobias Finch's surviving sister, who reveals he vanished in 1994 after copying something for Aldous. His last letter mentions 'a confession worth two graves.' Beat: the mystery gains a second missing body and a human cost.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Caspian Zephyrine POV. Charming and cornered, Caspian recounts the night his grandfather supposedly died, offering an alibi so polished Emrys can hear the rehearsal in it. He warns her off with courtesy that feels like a blade. Beat: first antagonist pressure, reader doubt planted.

chapters.title: The Millrace at Low Water
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Dredging records and wading the millrace herself, she finds a 1994 watch fob fused with stone. The police chief, an old friend, tells her to drop it or lose her practice. Beat: isolation deepens; the law itself becomes an obstacle.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating archive fragments (Finch's notes) with Emrys POV. The founding families' fortune traces to a drowned business partner, Elias Thorn, whose death was ruled accidental — and whose daughter was adopted out under a new name. Beat: the theme of inheritance as theft crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Woman Named Wren
chapters.summary: Wren POV. A bookbinder in the next county feels watched since the exhumation made the news. Emrys arrives asking about her adoption; Wren lies badly about a locket she wears. Beat: introduce the living heir, wary and wounded, denying what she suspects.

chapters.title: Silence at the Vane House
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Matriarch Odile Vane — sharp, dying, amused — admits the families have kept one secret for thirty years but refuses to say which, warning that the last person who asked is 'under the millrace.' Beat: a gothic gatekeeper who confirms danger without confirming facts.

chapters.title: The Glove in the Coffin
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Forensics on the rotted glove dates it to the 1990s — meaning the coffin was empty all along, and the exhumation was meant to be discovered. Someone wanted the grave opened. Beat: reversal; the crime isn't hiding a body, it's staging an absence.

chapters.title: Caspian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, breaking into the Zephyrine boathouse. She finds Caspian's private ledger: payments to the gravedigger, to a records clerk, and — chillingly — to the woman who filed her three 'accident' cases. Her solved deaths connect here. Beat: personal stakes detonate; the past cases were cover fires.

chapters.title: Wren's Locket
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Pressed by Emrys, Wren opens the locket: a miniature of Aldous and a scrap in Finch's hand naming her father Elias Thorn. She admits she received an anonymous letter last month telling her to attend the dinner. Beat: grief and fury; the heir becomes a player, not a prize.

chapters.title: The Gravedigger Confesses Halfway
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The terrified gravedigger admits he was paid to report the coffin empty only if anyone ever checked — a thirty-year insurance policy. Before he can name his employer, his workshop burns overnight. Beat: escalation into violence; time is running out.

chapters.title: Two Graves, One Body
chapters.summary: Emrys and Wren POV alternating. Following Finch's letter, they probe beneath the deconsecrated chapel and find a second coffin: Tobias Finch himself, and beside him bones wearing Aldous Zephyrine's signet ring. The founder never left town. Beat: the central reveal — Aldous was murdered in 1994 and hidden by his own family.

chapters.title: The Alibis Unravel
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reconstructing the night, she tests each heir's alibi against weather records, tide tables, and the ledger. All the polished stories collapse except one — Caspian's, which now fits too perfectly because he built it from his father's confession. Beat: deduction climax approaching; suspicion pivots across generations.

chapters.title: Odile's Deathbed Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile Vane POV. Dying, the matriarch dictates the truth: her generation covered up Aldous's murder by his son to protect the family name, and Finch was killed for witnessing it. She gives Emrys the original confession page Caspian has been hunting. Beat: the moral weight of inherited silence; a flawed woman chooses truth at the end.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The confession page vanishes from her office; her assistant is found unhurt but paid off and gone. Caspian calls, courteous, inviting her to the anniversary dinner as his guest. Beat: darkest hour — evidence gone, ally turned, trap accepted.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Under crystal and candlelight, Emrys rises during the toast and lays out the murder, the swapped coffins, and the ledger before the assembled founders' descendants. Caspian counters smoothly until Wren stands and claims her name aloud: Thorn. Beat: public climax; identity claimed as testimony.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Emrys and Wren POV. Caspian flees to the millrace to retrieve the final proof and is caught by Emrys and the chief, who finally chooses conscience over career. The families beg for quiet; instead they fund Wren's claim and Finch's memorial. Beat: resolution through restitution rather than mere arrest.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. On a gray morning, Aldous Zephyrine and Tobias Finch are buried properly, Wren reading the true will aloud. The town's myth dies politely; its people begin again. Beat: elegiac closure; justice done outside the courtroom, inside the community.

chapters.title: Zephyrine's Confession
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, coda. Alone with the case file, Emrys writes her own confession — how she solved four deaths and stayed silent — and mails it to the chief, then signs her long-buried birth name beneath Winterbourne for the first time. Beat: the theme turns inward; identity, like inheritance, must finally be claimed.
